summary:
Turn 15 corrected the accept-round observation and submitted it as a new check on the same unit, replacing the artifact whose property had been shown to watch the wrong round.

What was wrong before. The earlier accept-round property read acceptOKs while the recovery had only restarted phase 1: the harness delivered the restart's PreAccept and its reply but never the Accept and its AcceptReply, so accept_oks 0 to 0 measured the phase-1 reply. That artifact's violated outcome was an observation artefact.

Correction. The harness now drives every queued round explicitly and in order (the Prepare/PrepareReply resolution, the phase-1 restart's PreAccept and its reply, then the Accept the recoverer queues and its reply), re-reading InstanceSpace after each delivery because startPhase1 replaces the record object, and it emits a canonical recovery_outcome event with the recoverer's committed status and command, the peer's committed command, the accept count and a vectors_match flag. The corrected local construction run shows the accept round completing (accept_oks 0 to 1, reply_counted true) and the recoverer committing the instance with a NOOP command while the peer holds a PUT: recoverer_committed true, peer_committed_command PUT, vectors_match false, with a Commit broadcast visible in the trailing diagnostic out_codes.

New artifact. The plan keeps the reviewed adoption property and its prerequisite and replaces the unreached accept-round property with an outcome property on the new event (assertion: if the recoverer commits the instance, it must commit the vector the already-committed replica holds), sharing the same identity and admission alias, with grounding in the resolution, accept and commit handlers, updated semantic-changes notes and uncertainties. The formal outcome is left to the trusted runner and to a fresh correspondence review; the previously confirmed adoption finding keeps its own basis untouched.

Why this matters. If the runner reproduces it, the consequence is not a blocked catch-up but two different committed values for one instance (NOOP at the recovering replica, PUT at the replica that already committed), which is an agreement violation rather than a progress failure. That reframes the importance of the finding, and it is recorded as an observation to be confirmed rather than asserted. No map object was changed and no requirement, premise or earlier observation was weakened.
